cold_email.subject: Interest in Full Time Educator / South Galena Street, Aspen CO — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Full Time Educator / South Galena Street, Aspen CO opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Urology Laboratory Research Assistant / Urology / SOM / HU2642 opportunity with Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine at Virginia Commonwealth University School of Medicine.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate, Library — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Third Bridge Group Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate, Library opportunity with Third Bridge Group at Third Bridge Group.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate - Modeling, Simulation, and Software Development - Entry-Level — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Institute for Defense Analyses Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate - Modeling, Simulation, and Software Development - Entry-Level opportunity with Institute for Defense Analyses at Institute for Defense Analyses.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Park, #602 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Park, #602 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Park, #602 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Park, #602 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Hills, #478 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Hills, #478 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineering Mfg Liaison I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear General Atomics Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineering Mfg Liaison I opportunity with General Atomics at General Atomics.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Full-Time Educator / Contract Through February 2027 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Full-Time Educator / Contract Through February 2027 opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Administrative Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pyramid Global Hospitality Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Assistant opportunity with Pyramid Global Hospitality at Pyramid Global Hospitality.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Master's University Grad Machine Learning Engineer 2027 (USA) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pinterest Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Master's University Grad Machine Learning Engineer 2027 (USA) opportunity with Pinterest at Pinterest.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Student Finance Coordinator (Contact Center) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Kaplan Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Student Finance Coordinator (Contact Center) opportunity with Kaplan at Kaplan.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Assistant Clinical — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Arkansas Children's Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Assistant Clinical opportunity with Arkansas Children's at Arkansas Children's.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Scientist, Arrayed Screening, Alzheimer's Disease Initiative
jobs.description: About Arc Institute Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco. Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone. Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action: Virtual Cell Initiative : Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets, accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials. Alzheimer's Disease Initiative : Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes. More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding. About the position We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Scientist with a strong background in stem cell biology and high-throughput screening to join the Molecular Engineering team within the Genome Engineering Technology Center at the Arc Institute. In this role, you will lead the optimization, scale-up, and execution of arrayed perturbation screens in 2D human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived microglia. This includes refining and adapting microglia differentiation protocols for high-throughput screening, validating their reproducibility and compatibility with diverse perturbations and readouts, and establishing robust workflows that can transition to automated platforms. In this highly collaborative, cross-functional role, you will partner with researchers across Arc’s Tech Centers and Core Labs to drive the process development, validation, and execution of these screening pipelines, directly enabling Arc’s Alzheimer’s Disease Initiative (ADI), an ambitious effort to identify and drug rational therapeutic targets for neurodegenerative disorders About you You are passionate about science and excited about answering questions related to functional genomics, genome engineering technology development, and complex human diseases. You are creative and excited to try new ways of tackling problems beyond the techniques and approaches you’re already familiar with. You have a systematic, process-oriented mindset and take pride in building workflows that are reproducible, scalable, and ready for automation. You understand the importance of collaboration and thrive when working with a diverse team of scientists. You have a deep commitment to data quality while working in a fast-paced environment. Your organizational skills enable you to manage multiple concurrent projects, and your curiosity and creativity drive you to continuous learning and innovation. You have high standards for experimental design and data analysis while moving fast and efficiently to keep projects on track. In this position you will Design, lead and execute the adaptation and validation of 2D hPSC-derived microglia differentiation for high-throughput arrayed perturbation screens, optimizing protocols as needed to establish scalable, reproducible, and automation-ready workflows. Define quality control metrics and acceptance criteria across differentiation and screen execution to ensure robust, interpretable transcriptomic and functional readouts at scale. Collaborate with experimental and computational teams across Arc to establish compatibility with diverse perturbations and downstream readouts, and work closely with automation engineers to implement and rigorously validate automated workflows. Contribute to additional pooled and arrayed genetic perturbation screening efforts across the Molecular Engineering team, supporting workflows that advance Arc’s Alzheimer’s Disease Initiative. Present findings at internal meetings and external conferences, and contribute to scientific publications. Stay current on developments in genome engineering, functional genomics, and high-throughput screening, actively seeking opportunities for innovation and technology adoption. Requirements Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Bioengineering, Genetics, Biochemistry, or a related field. 0–5 years of post-PhD research experience (industry or academia). Experience with hPSC culture and differentiation; immune cell differentiation experience highly desirable. Experience with CRISPR-Cas9 or other genome editing/perturbation techniques (e.g., CRISPRi/a). Experience designing, executing, and troubleshooting arrayed screening workflows; experience carrying out high-throughput workflows strongly preferred. Proficiency with computational tools for analyzing genomics data (Python, R, or similar). Strong project management skills with the ability to plan, execute, and deliver results on time. Demonstrated ability to work both independently and in a highly collaborative, multidisciplinary environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Benchling or similar LIMS systems. Hands-on experience with developing protocols intended for lab automation and linking/tracking associated processes and materials within a LIMS system. Experience with process development or scaling of cell-based workflows. The base salary range for this position is $128,500 to $159,000. These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors. In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). The CCGP is a program designed to offer multi-year cash grants providing for a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute. As soon as reasonably practical after your start date, you will receive a grant letter describing the terms of your award under the CCGP.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Scientist, Arrayed Screening, Alzheimer's Disease Initiative — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Arc Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Scientist, Arrayed Screening, Alzheimer's Disease Initiative opportunity with Arc Institute at Arc Institute.

I am especially interested in the group's effort to integrate multi-omic and clinical data with AI for biomarker and therapeutic discovery. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in bioinformatics, pipeline development, and an LLM-assisted competency-mapping project has made me especially interested in rigorous, interpretable AI for biomedical data.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Technical GTM Recruiter
jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is seeking a Technical GTM Recruiter to support hiring across our technical go-to-market organization. You’ll partner with technical GTM recruiters and hiring leaders to build strong pipelines across Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Applied AI, AI Outcome Leads, Technical Support Engineering, and related customer-facing technical roles. You’ll own full-cycle recruiting for assigned junior-level searches and, as you build proficiency, expand your ownership based on business need and performance. You will: Own full-cycle recruiting for assigned junior-level technical GTM roles, from intake and sourcing through screening, interview management, closing support, and offer coordination. Support sourcing for higher-level technical GTM positions by building role-specific talent maps, identifying target companies and talent pools, and developing prioritized outreach strategies. Partner with recruiters and hiring leaders to calibrate candidate profiles, define must-have signals, and maintain clear evaluation and pass-through criteria. Source through LinkedIn Recruiter, Gem, referrals, direct outreach, and other channels to build thoughtful, diverse pipelines for technical GTM teams. Coordinate and manage recruiting processes with clear candidate communication, timely feedback, accurate Greenhouse stage movement, and effective use of Modern Loop and related tools. Support recruiter screens, intake preparation, interview debriefs, and offer coordination across the recruiting lifecycle. Deliver a consistent candidate experience through clear communication, expectation-setting, timely follow-up, and effective representation of Glean and the role. Track pipeline activity, pass-through rates, and process progress; surface risks early and help the team take action. About you: You have approximately 2+ years of recruiting experience, ideally including full-cycle recruiting or direct exposure to technical GTM, customer-facing technical, or adjacent roles. You have demonstrated sourcing judgment and can translate a calibrated profile into a focused talent map, outreach plan, and qualified slate. You have owned part of the recruiting lifecycle and are ready to manage assigned junior-level searches end to end. You are organized, metrics-minded, and disciplined about ATS data, process milestones, and stakeholder follow-through. You communicate clearly and build trust with candidates, recruiters, coordinators, and hiring leaders. You learn quickly, welcome feedback, and apply structured processes while operating with urgency. You are comfortable using data and recruiting technology, and take pride in accurate execution and a strong candidate experience. Location: This role is hybrid, based 4 days a week out of our Mountain View or San Francisco offices. Compensation & Benefits: The standard base salary range for this position is $110,000 - $135,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We’re committed to building and sustaining a diverse, inclusive workplace. We strive to attract and retain people with a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we do not discriminate on the basis of gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants: Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or other privacy laws may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . By clicking “Submit Application,” I confirm that I have read the Global Data Privacy Notice and the Applicant Arbitration Agreement , and I agree to the terms.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Production Engineering, FinOps
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. OUR TEAMS Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does. Right now, we operate across five areas: - Compute — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts. - Storage — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement. - Developer Infrastructure — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost. - Compliance Platform — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements. - Reliability Platform — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build. WHAT YOU'LL DO As a FinOps Specialist within Production Engineering, you’ll help Ramp make better decisions about infrastructure spend – from resource usage and cloud commitments to vendor contracts and new investments. You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results. This is a senior individual contributor role. Day to day, you will: - Set direction for infrastructure cost management. Identify the highest-impact opportunities across Ramp, establish priorities with Production Engineering leadership and partner teams, and build a roadmap that balances immediate savings with lasting improvements. - Understand and explain our spend. Investigate costs across AWS, observability, and AI providers. Connect changes to usage, architecture, customer growth, and engineering decisions, and help teams distinguish expected investment from avoidable waste. - Embed with teams early. Partner with product and infrastructure teams during design and planning. Help them evaluate cost implications, model how systems will scale, and make informed tradeoffs before committing to an architecture or vendor. - Build forecasts we can defend. Work with engineers to understand upcoming launches, migrations, and capacity needs. Translate those plans into financial models that explain expected spend, key assumptions, and uncertainty. - Shape commitment and vendor strategy. Model cloud discounts, commitment levels, payment structures, and renewal scenarios. Partner with Finance, Procurement, and infrastructure leaders to develop negotiation strategies and carry them through vendor discussions. - Drive optimization across the company. Proactively identify opportunities that span teams, propose a path forward, align engineering owners and technical program managers, and stay involved through implementation and verified savings. - Make cost visible and actionable. Partner with DevInfra to build attribution, dashboards, anomaly detection, and self-service tools that let teams understand and manage their costs. Establish reusable approaches that make cost awareness part of how Ramp builds, and work toward clearer service and product unit economics. - Evaluate new infrastructure investments. Build models for decisions such as buying versus renting capacity, changing providers, or adopting new infrastructure. Make the financial implications and technical assumptions clear. - Use AI to investigate and build. Use AI tools and coding agents to analyze data, create dashboards and automations, navigate infrastructure code, and develop proposed changes with engineering partners. Help improve the tools and workflows that make cost management repeatable. WHAT WE LOOK FOR We don’t hire for a checklist. We hire for the judgment and ownership that make someone effective in this role. The mindset we’re looking for: - You follow the question through. When a bill changes, you want to understand what happened, whether it makes sense, and what to do about it. - You have high agency. You identify opportunities without waiting for an assignment, investigate independently, and bring a recommendation. When progress depends on other teams, you find the right partners and drive the work forward. - You think in systems and tradeoffs. You connect technical decisions to financial outcomes and weigh savings against reliability, performance, engineering time, and flexibility. - You look for the underlying cause. When you uncover unexpected spend or an inefficient process, you investigate what allowed it to happen and improve the tooling, decisions, or practices that will prevent it from recurring. - You connect efficiency to customer outcomes. You partner closely with engineering teams to understand their goals and make cost tradeoffs that help Ramp serve customers reliably and scale sustainably. You pursue savings with a clear understanding of their impact on performance, reliability, and the team’s ability to deliver. - You make complex things understandable. You can discuss financial models with Finance and infrastructure choices with engineers, and help both make decisions together. - You own the outcome. You set priorities, build alignment, and follow through to implementation and measured results. You turn what you learn into tools and practices that help teams make better decisions themselves. Experience profile: - Experience improving infrastructure economics in a growing technology organization, with examples of decisions you influenced and measurable results you helped deliver. - Strong financial modeling and forecasting skills. You can translate engineering roadmaps, customer growth, migrations, and new infrastructure investments into future spend scenarios. You make assumptions and uncertainty explicit, explain variances, and update forecasts as plans evolve. - Experience planning large infrastructure contracts and commitments. You can model usage over multi-year terms, compare pricing and payment structures, and balance savings against overcommitment risk and flexibility. You’ve helped shape commitment levels, renewal timing, and negotiation strategy with Finance, Procurement, and engineering leaders. - Working knowledge of cloud billing and pricing, including cost allocation, commitment discounts, payment structures, and the relationship between usage and cost. AWS experience is especially relevant. - Strong technical fluency. You can reason about compute, storage, networking, and managed services, and navigate Terraform or similar infrastructure-as-code tools to understand how systems are configured. You can investigate technical questions independently, connect infrastructure choices to cost, and work with engineers on concrete changes. - Experience with cost attribution and analysis. You can connect infrastructure spend to teams, services, products, and usage drivers, including shared resources. You work directly with cost and usage data, reconcile conflicting sources, and develop practical allocation methods with clear assumptions. - A record of initiating and driving work across teams, from identifying an opportunity and building the case to coordinating implementation and validating the result. - Practical experience using AI tools and coding agents to analyze data, build dashboards or automations, and investigate technical questions. You can evaluate their output and recognize when deeper engineering review is needed. Relevant backgrounds include FinOps, infrastructure finance, strategic sourcing, analytics, data, and infrastructure engineering. A software engineering background is welcome, but not required. Bonus (not required): - Deep experience with AWS Cost and Usage Reports, Savings Plans, or Reserved Instances. - Cost management for Datadog, other observability platforms, or AI providers. - Product unit economics or infrastructure accounting classifications. - Financial analysis of large migrations, dedicated compute, or data center investments. - Experience in fintech, payments, or regulated industries, with an understanding of how compliance, security, and data residency requirements shape infrastructure choices and costs. BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL) - Flexible PTO - Centralized home-office equipment ordering - Health and wellness stipend - Budget for intra-office travel - Weekly coffee stipend UNITED STATES - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents - One Medical annual membership - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp…

jobs.title: Geotechnical Engineer, Data Center Development
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is developing data center infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. The team brings together site development, civil and structural engineering, utilities, construction, commissioning, and operations to move campuses from early evaluation through delivery. About the Role We’re looking for a Geotechnical Engineer to help evaluate, plan, and deliver data center campuses. You’ll translate subsurface conditions into practical recommendations for site selection, campus design, construction, and long-term reliability. The work spans early due diligence through design review and field execution, with a focus on identifying ground-related risks early and helping teams make informed decisions. Key Responsibilities - Develop, update, and maintain geotechnical and geoenvironmental scopes of work, Owner’s Project Requirements (OPRs), technical specifications, and engineering standards for site due diligence and design phases, ensuring consistency across data center and power infrastructure projects while supporting risk mitigation, cost optimization, and accelerated project deliver - Plan and review geotechnical investigations, including borings, in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and groundwater monitoring. - Evaluate subsurface conditions and develop recommendations for foundations, settlement, seismic design, earthwork, subgrades, pavements, retaining systems, slopes, and groundwater management. - Assess geotechnical risks during site selection and due diligence, including variable ground conditions, liquefaction, expansive or compressible soils, karst, settlement, and constructability constraints. - Review geotechnical reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, and consultant deliverables for technical quality and consistency with project requirements. - Partner with civil, structural, architectural, utilities, and construction teams to integrate geotechnical recommendations into campus plans and building designs. - Support permitting and agency coordination by providing clear technical documentation and responding to review comments. - Provide construction-phase support, including review of submittals and field conditions, evaluation of differing site conditions, and recommendations for corrective actions. - Help establish consistent geotechnical standards, investigation scopes, design criteria, and risk documentation across projects and sites. - Communicate ground-related risks, assumptions, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders. - Review construction documents for foundation systems, earthwork, and ground improvement solutions for data center buildings, equipment yards, and power generation plants to ensure compliance with owner requirements, applicable codes, and project-specific geotechnical recommendations. Qualifications - A degree in civil engineering, geological engineering, geotechnical engineering, or a related discipline. - Professional experience in geotechnical engineering for large, complex infrastructure, industrial, mission-critical, or campus-scale projects. - Strong technical judgment across subsurface investigation, foundation recommendations, earthwork, settlement, groundwater, and seismic considerations. - Experience reviewing consultant work and translating findings into actionable design and construction recommendations. - Familiarity with geotechnical analysis methods and common engineering tools used for foundation, slope, settlement, and earthwork evaluation. - The ability to work effectively with consultants, contractors, designers, and project teams while maintaining clear ownership of technical decisions. - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain uncertainty and risk. Preferred Skills - Experience supporting data centers, power generation, advanced manufacturing, or other critical infrastructure. - Experience with large campus developments, phased construction, and multiple building or utility packages. - Familiarity with local permitting, building-code, and geotechnical design requirements across different jurisdictions. - Professional Engineer license, or ability to obtain licensure where required. - Experience developing repeatable technical standards or reviewing work across a portfolio of sites. cold_email.body:
Dear OpenAI Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Geotechnical Engineer, Data Center Development opportunity with OpenAI at OpenAI.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: The Medical Science Liaison (MSL) is a field-based scientific expert responsible for engaging healthcare providers, generating insights, and supporting Medical Affairs priorities across Natera’s oncology portfolio, including our personalized minimal residual disease (MRD) testing. This role focuses on building strong scientific relationships, delivering clear and accurate education, and bringing back actionable insights from the field. You will own your territory, make decisions independently, and deliver clear clinical data to providers to help them make better-informed decisions. Territory : North Texas, Arkansas, Oklahoma PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Establish and maintain scientific relationships with healthcare providers and key opinion leaders (KOLs) within a defined territory. Deliver accurate, balanced, and clinically relevant education on Natera’s oncology products and data. Deliver on territory plans aligned to Medical Affairs priorities. Identify and communicate field insights, including treatment trends, unmet needs, and competitive dynamics. Respond to unsolicited medical inquiries in a timely, compliant, and scientifically rigorous manner. Support execution of Medical Affairs initiatives including advisory boards and medical education programs. Maintain a strong understanding of disease states, clinical data, and the evolving oncology landscape. Collaborate directly with Sales, Marketing, and R&D to move work forward without relying on rigid processes. Maintain medical independence and strict compliance, always keeping the patient at the center of your work. Support and coordinate clinical trial and research initiatives at academic institutions and study sites. Meet all metrics as assigned and complete appropriate documentation and tracking of field visits, insights, and research opportunities. Travel extensively (over 60%) as required. QUALIFICATIONS: Advanced healthcare/scientific degree preferred (Ph.D., Pharm.D, M.D., D.N.P.). Master’s degree required. Diagnostic, IVD, or device experience preferred. Must live within the assigned territory. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Clear communicator and independent thinker. Ability to work remotely while maintaining a strong teamwork ethic. Make evidence-based decisions quickly and operate with urgency to get meaningful products to clinicians without compromising quality. Use strategic thinking to contribute to product, departmental, and organizational plans and goals. Adapt quickly when priorities shift and solve problems rather than waiting for structure. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to read, interpret, and convey complex scientific information. PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT: Remote position requiring frequent sitting, standing, walking, and daily computer use. Extensive travel required. Requires the ability to communicate over the telephone and read printed material. Duties may require working outside normal working hours (evenings and weekends). Complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training, and security training within the first 30 days of hire. Reasonable accommodations available for individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $137,400 — $171,700 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! cold_email.subject: Interest in Medical Science Liaison — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Medical Science Liaison opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Solutions Consultant, Post Sales, Strategic
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE Solutions Consultant, Post-Sales at Ramp partner with Account Management to deepen and expand relationships with existing Ramp customers. You'll act as the technical and financial subject matter expert across the customer lifecycle — running product demonstrations to expand customers onto new Ramp products, while bringing the depth needed to resolve complex ERP integrations, configuration challenges, and technical blockers. You'll collaborate closely with Account Managers to assess requirements, design scalable solutions, and ensure fast time-to-value as customers grow with Ramp. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value to the customers. This role requires strong technical skills — comfort with APIs, ERP systems, and integration architecture — paired with the communication ability to translate complexity into clear business value for finance and operations stakeholders. This role is specifically focused on Strategic Enterprise customers, supporting large, complex organizations with multi-entity environments, advanced ERP integrations, and highly customized financial workflows. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Partner with Account Managers to demonstrate new Ramp products and features to existing customers, building the business case for expansion through customized demos and workflow illustrations - Evaluate customer requirements for expansion opportunities, assessing fit through use-case analysis, ROI assessments, and technical scoping - Design and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture — including when and how to use APIs, ERP integrations, and HRIS connectors — based on each customer's existing systems and workflows - Act as a technical advisor to customers and internal teams, guiding integration, configuration, and system design decisions without writing code directly - Troubleshoot ERP and integration blockers, and guide customers through complex configuration decisions across NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion, and others - Support Account Managers on technical workstreams, ensuring faster time-to-value during product rollouts and expansions - Be a subject matter expert across accounting systems and integration partners; advocate for integration development in line with customer needs alongside Product and Partners - Influence Ramp's product roadmap by channeling customer pain points and feedback to Product and Engineering teams - Contribute to internal documentation, tooling, and knowledge bases that scale Ramp's ability to support integration use cases across a growing customer base WHAT YOU NEED - 4+ years in Solutions Consulting, Technical Consulting, Implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role in SaaS or fintech - Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field - Hands-on familiarity with ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion) and finance/accounting workflows - Comfort with APIs, integration logic, and system architecture — and the ability to explain those concepts clearly to finance and operations stakeholders - Experience running product demonstrations and translating complex technical capabilities into clear business value - Strong communication skills: able to guide customers toward scalable approaches and diplomatically steer conversations when requests are misaligned with product capabilities or best practices - Collaborative mindset; effective working cross-functionally with Account Management, Product, and Engineering - Thrives in ambiguity and fast-paced environments; highly organized, ownership-oriented, and resourceful as Ramp scales its upmarket motion BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL) - Flexible PTO - Centralized home-office equipment ordering - Health and wellness stipend - Budget for intra-office travel - Weekly coffee stipend UNITED STATES - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents - One Medical annual membership - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay - Pet insurance - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) CANADA - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health UNITED KINGDOM - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. OTHER NOTICES Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com http://Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process. jobs.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is seeking a Solutions Engineer to help enterprise customers in the Western US connect complex business and technical challenges to practical outcomes with Glean. You will partner with Account Executives across the sales cycle, leading discovery, tailored demonstrations, technical evaluations, security conversations, and business-value discussions. You will: Partner with Account Executives to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles with C-level executives Create and demo custom environments based off of customer industry and line of business Run and manage a technical POC cycle Perform customer facing activities including technical discovery calls Lead security based conversations to make customers comfortable with Glean’s security posture Work cross functionally with product and engineering to deliver customer request and be a voice of the customer Develop ROI and business justification reports and presentations About you: 5+ years of sales engineering or solution consulting experience in a SaaS organization Bachelor's degree in CS or a related field Excellent written and verbal communication skills Highly motivated, driven and self-starting individual with a growth mindset Ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment Clear examples of partnering with AEs to run technical deal cycles with Enterprise customers A consultative approach with solving your customer’s business challenges and having a track record of successfully overcoming technical and security objections Familiarity with any cloud environment (GCP, AWS, Azure) Proficiency in Python, Java, or MCPs is preferred Ability to configure, monitor and maintain API based integrations Owns technical troubleshooting Location: This role is based out of out of our SF office in a hybrid capacity. Compensation & Benefits: The OTE range for this position is $180,000 - $230,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants: Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or other privacy laws may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . jobs.title: Lead Solutions Engineer | Upmarket, ANZ
jobs.description: Who are we? At HubSpot, we empower thousands of businesses around the world to grow better. If you thrive in solving complex challenges, love learning, and enjoy collaborating with a global team, this role could be your next great opportunity. Our Australian office is based in Sydney, but we’re equally happy for you to join our team as a remote employee. For more information, check out: Hybrid at HubSpot AI is changing how businesses buy. Buyers arrive informed, and they want to see their own business running in HubSpot, with proof it will deliver results, before they commit. HubSpot's customer platform connects customer context, Breeze AI agents and a unified CRM, so growing businesses get real outcomes, not just new software. What’s the role As a Lead Solutions Engineer working with our Upmarket sales org (Midmarket/Corp), you'll partner with Account Executives to show mid-sized businesses what HubSpot can do for them, then prove it. You'll lead discovery, tell outcome-led stories through tailored demos, and build lightweight working proofs so customers can try their solution before they buy. This is a pre-sales role, not a software engineering role. It suits people who enjoy business conversations as much as building with technology, and who want to grow their technical, customer, communication and sales skills fast. If you love storytelling and building, you thrive at the intersection of business and technology, and want to help write the playbook for how software is bought next, this role is for you. What you'll do Work a varied pipeline of new and existing-customer deals alongside Account Executives, from discovery to the technical win. Lead discovery to understand each customer's goals, pain points, current systems and requirements. Tell compelling, outcome-led stories (via demos and product led experiences) that show customers how their business can be reimagined in HubSpot Partner with Account Executives to map the technical buying committee, competitive landscape and path to a decision. Design HubSpot solutions that fit the customer's processes and connect sensibly with the tools they already use. Build lightweight proofs of concept with AI tools, Breeze AI agents and HubSpot configuration, scoped to clear use cases and success criteria, and help customers try them hands-on. Answer ad-hoc or RFP-based technical, security and integration questions, collaborating with specialists and partners as needed. Help your AE shape the business case and value story for the customer's first use cases. Prove the outcome via use-case roadmap and a consumption plan that sizes the first commitment. Keep what you show realistic to deploy, and hand over clear context to solution architects, onboarding teams and partners so customers start strong and realise value fast. Lead by example: mentor other SEs, run initiatives, share field feedback and reusable assets with the team to improve our playbooks and product. Travel occasionally to customer sites. What you’ll bring: Experience in a customer-facing technical or consultative role for a SaaS product, such as solutions engineering, technical consulting, implementation, onboarding or customer success with a track record of winning complex deals or delivering solutions that moved business results. Humility and a growth mindset: the world of SaaS is changing fast and there is a lot of ambiguity. Nobody can know everything. You’re happy to lead from the front where needed and offer your support to team mates while equally being open to learn from others. Art-of-the-Possible Storytelling: Ability to turn a customer's goals into a compelling, outcome-led vision of their business reimagined in HubSpot. Outstanding communication skills & stakeholder management - both internal and external: you feel equally comfortable talking to IT as to C-suite, you can tell a story about business outcomes that resonates with stakeholders at various levels and you can successfully navigate multiple internal & external stakeholders. Curiosity in discovery: you ask good questions, dig deep into business, financial and individual pain, and pick up on needs customers don't explicitly share. cold_email.subject: Interest in Software Engineer III — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Software Engineer III opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
